what_is_overlap.h2: What is Mutual Fund Overlap and Why Does It Matter?
what_is_overlap.body: Mutual fund overlap occurs when two or more funds in your portfolio hold the same stocks. While some overlap is normal (especially in large-cap funds), high overlap can lead to over-concentration and 'diworsification' â€” where you think you are diversified but are actually holding the same underlying assets. This calculator helps you uncover that hidden risk. Smart diversification is crucial for long-term wealth building. Use our retirement corpus calculator to understand how your diversified portfolio should grow to meet your financial goals.

how_it_works.h2: How Our Mutual Fund Overlap Calculator Works
how_it_works.body:
Our tool compares the holdings of the funds you select and calculates the weighted overlap. This metric tells you what percentage of your portfolio is duplicated between two funds, based on the smaller weight for each common stock.

Example: If Fund A holds 5% in ICICI Bank and Fund B holds 6%, the overlap contribution from that stock is 5% (the minimum of the two). We sum this for all common shares to get the total weighted overlap.

interpreting_results.h2: How to Interpret Your Overlap Score
interpreting_results.body:
• Low (0-15%): Good diversification. The funds have distinct strategies.
  • Moderate (15-30%): Common for funds in the same category (e.g., large-cap). Review to ensure you are comfortable with the shared exposure.
  • High (30-50%): Significant overlap. You may be paying two sets of fees for the same stocks. Consider consolidating.
  • Very High (>50%): The funds are practically clones. Replacing one to improve diversification is highly recommended.

what_to_do.h2: What to Do If You Have High Overlap
what_to_do.body: If you find a high overlap, don't panic. Consider replacing one of the funds with another that has a different strategy or market-cap focus. For example, if two large-cap funds overlap, you might switch one to a mid-cap or a sector-specific fund to achieve true diversification. Our mutual fund screener can help you find funds with different strategies. Also explore FD vs PPF options and PPF for more conservative allocations. Use our tax regime calculator to understand the tax implications of any fund switches, and our loan optimizer to manage any debt before increasing investments.

faqs.q: How is mutual fund overlap calculated?
faqs.a: We calculate the weighted overlap by summing the minimum weight of each common stock held by two funds. The formula is: Î£ min(Weight_Fund_A, Weight_Fund_B) for all common stocks. This helps identify diversification gaps in your portfolio. Compare with our mutual fund screener to find complementary funds.

faqs.q: Is 30% overlap in mutual funds bad?
faqs.a: An overlap of 30% is considered high. While not necessarily 'bad,' it suggests you may be paying two expense ratios for very similar holdings, which reduces diversification. It is worth reviewing if you need both funds in your portfolio. For alternative investments, check our FD vs PPF calculator, PPF, or NPS for tax-efficient savings.

faqs.q: How do you check overlap in mutual funds?
faqs.a: Simply select 2 to 5 Indian equity funds from the dropdown menus in our calculator. The tool will automatically fetch the latest holdings data and calculate the pairwise overlap for you.

faqs.q: Which type of funds have the most overlap?
faqs.a: Large-cap and index funds tend to have the most overlap because they often track similar benchmarks (like the Nifty 50 or Sensex) and invest in the same set of top blue-chip companies. Use our mutual fund screener to find mid-cap or sector funds for diversification. Plan your complete portfolio with our retirement corpus calculator.

faqs.q: How do I build a diversified portfolio using this calculator?
faqs.a: Start by analyzing your current funds with this overlap calculator. Identify high-overlap pairs and consider replacing one with a fund from a different category (e.g., mid-cap, small-cap, or sector-specific). Use our mutual fund screener to find alternatives, balance with FD or PPF for stability, and plan using our retirement corpus calculator.

faqs.q: Should I completely avoid overlap in my mutual fund portfolio?
faqs.a: No, some overlap is natural and healthy. The key is managing it strategically. Diversification across fund types (large-cap, mid-cap, small-cap, debt, international) with manageable overlap is ideal. Use our mutual fund screener to find complementary funds, check tax implications with tax regime calculator, and plan comprehensively with our retirement corpus calculator.

faqs.q: How does mutual fund overlap relate to overall financial planning?
faqs.a: Portfolio overlap affects your overall diversification and risk management. If overlapped, you have less true diversification and higher concentration risk. Balance mutual fund investments with other vehicles like PPF, FD, NPS, and insurance (use our LIC premium calculator). Plan your complete financial picture using our retirement corpus calculator and tax regime calculator.

methodology.body:
Data Sources: Our holdings data is sourced from publicly available scheme documents and updated periodically. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee it. Always verify with official AMC factsheets. Last Updated: Aug 2025.

Matching Logic: Holdings are matched first by their stock ticker (e.g., 'RELIANCE'). If a ticker is not available, we use a normalized company name (e.g., 'reliance industries' after removing 'Ltd', 'Inc', etc.). Non-equity holdings like 'Cash', 'Tri-party repo', or 'Net Receivables' are excluded from the calculation based on a regex match for common terms.
